exposure: first trimester placental markers (Pregnancy Associated Plasma Protein A, free b-Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (HCG), mean pulsatility index of uterine arteries (UtA PI), placental volume, crown-rump length (CRL))
cohort: 1052 healthy women with singleton autologous pregnancies (523 male, 529 female), enrolled at 11-13(+6) weeks gestational age.
finding: The study found crucial differences in prenatal development and placentation between male and female fetuses, with female fetuses having a lower risk of preterm delivery and male fetuses exhibiting higher birth weight and lower arterial cord pH values.
mod_finding: Male fetuses showed lower arterial cord pH values regardless of the delivery mode, even after excluding planned cesarean sections.
